reasoning_notes.reasoning: A moderate opening wage balances a chance to win labor against the margin earned if successful; adjust after observing B.
With equal revenues and split labor on ties, a middle wage balances winning profit against the cost of undercutting; I’ll use 10 as an initial probe.
Matching the observed wage preserves equal labor and earns 5; undercutting sacrifices margin, while raising risks earning nothing.
A matched 10 last round, so hold at 10 to preserve a half share at 5 profit while avoiding a costly bidding escalation.
B has matched 10 twice. Matching preserves the split and earns 5; undercutting gives up profit, while raising risks losing the labor.
A has matched 10 for two rounds. Holding preserves the shared outcome while avoiding a costly wage increase; undercutting would gain the unit but reduce profit from 5 to 4.
Matching B’s repeated wage of 10 preserves the equal split and earns 5; undercutting would sacrifice profit, while raising the wage would lose the labor.

B has chosen 10 repeatedly. Undercutting by one captures the full unit for profit 11, versus 5 from matching. With the horizon unknown, take the profitable undercut now.
